safetyPromise: Whatever you tell me, you won't be in trouble for telling me. We'll figure it out together.

cards.name: Relationships and crushes
cards.teenQuestion: How do you know if someone is good for you?
cards.whyNow: 10 of 12 teens in our survey wish their parents talked about relationships more, but only 1 of 12 learns mainly from parents. Friends and Instagram fill the gap.

firstLine.hinglish: Tumhare friends mein aajkal kisi ko koi pasand hai? Log kaise pata karte hain?
firstLine.hindi: तुम्हारे दोस्तों में आजकल किसी को कोई पसंद है? लोग कैसे पता करते हैं?
firstLine.english: Do any of your friends like someone these days? How do people figure it out?

followUps: What do you think makes someone good for you?
A lot of what we see in shows and online isn't how real relationships work. What feels fake to you?
say: You won't be in trouble for telling me.
It's normal to like someone. I liked people at your age too.
Real relationships aren't like what's shown in films or online. You can always ask me what's real.
avoid: Who is it? Tell me their name.
Jokes or teasing about crushes, even kind ones.

react.quiet: No rush. We can talk another time. I'm here whenever.
react.upset: I'm not checking up on you. I just want you to be able to come to me.
react.disagree: That's fair. Tell me how it looks from your side.
react.noTalk: Okay. Just know you can ask me anything, any time. No questions asked.

cards.getHelp: if your teen mentions being pressured, threatened, hurt, or asked for photos → see the help screen (Childline 1098, Cybercrime 1930).

cards.name: Stress and feelings
cards.teenQuestion: What do you do when everything feels like too much?
cards.whyNow: 81% of Indian school students say exams and results cause them anxiety. Teens in our survey said they want to be heard, not given advice straight away.
cards.whySource: NCERT mental health survey, 2022 · Raise teen survey, Oct 2026

firstLine.hinglish: Aajkal tumhare mann mein sabse zyada kya chal raha hai? Bas sunne ka mann hai, kuch solve nahi karna.
firstLine.hindi: आजकल तुम्हारे मन में सबसे ज़्यादा क्या चल रहा है? बस सुनने का मन है, कुछ सुलझाना नहीं है।
firstLine.english: What's taking up most of your headspace these days? I just want to listen, not fix anything.

followUps: What helps you feel a bit better when it gets heavy?
Is there anything I do that makes it harder?
say: You won't be in trouble for telling me.
That sounds really hard. Thank you for telling me.
You don't have to handle this alone.
avoid: Just don't think about it or "cheer up".
Comparing them with siblings, cousins or other kids.
Jumping straight to advice or solutions.

react.quiet: That's okay. We can just sit for a bit.
react.upset: I'm sorry. I'm not trying to push. I'm on your side.
react.disagree: You know your life better than I do. Help me understand.
react.noTalk: Okay. If you ever want to talk, even at midnight, I'm here.

cards.getHelp: if for weeks your teen isn't eating or sleeping properly, pulls away from everyone, or says life feels pointless → Tele-MANAS 14416 (free, 24×7). If they talk about hurting themselves → 112 now, and stay with them.
cards.sources: NCERT student mental health survey, 2022 · Raise teen survey, Oct 2026

cards.name: Friends and peer pressure
cards.teenQuestion: How do you say no to friends without losing them?
cards.whyNow: 10 of 12 teens in our survey learn mainly from friends, and 7 of 12 want parents to talk more about friends. They want questions about their world, not rules.

firstLine.hinglish: Tumhare group mein aajkal sab kis cheez ke peeche pade hain? Kya trend chal raha hai?
firstLine.hindi: तुम्हारे ग्रुप में आजकल सब किस चीज़ के पीछे पड़े हैं? क्या ट्रेंड चल रहा है?
firstLine.english: What's everyone in your group into these days? What's the big thing right now?

followUps: Has anyone in your group ever been pushed into something they didn't want to do?
What do you think makes someone a good friend?
say: You won't be in trouble for telling me.
Saying no to a friend is hard. Even adults find it hard.
If you ever need a way out, you can blame me. Say 'my parents won't allow it'.
avoid: Those friends are a bad influence.
Questions that sound like an interrogation (who, where, how late).
When I was your age… lectures.

react.quiet: No pressure. I was just curious about your world.
react.upset: I'm not judging your friends. I just want to know what your days are like.
react.disagree: Fair enough. What am I missing?
react.noTalk: Okay. My offer stands: you can always use me as your excuse.

cards.getHelp: if your teen is being bullied, threatened, or pushed into alcohol, drugs or anything risky → see the help screen (Childline 1098; Cybercrime 1930 if it's online).

cards.name: Online safety (photo blackmail, fake images, bullying)
cards.teenQuestion: What would you do if someone online asked for a photo?
cards.whyNow: 45% of Indian children who faced cyberbullying hid it from their parents. AI apps can now turn any normal photo into a fake one, and there have been cases in Indian colleges (IIIT Raipur, 2025).

firstLine.hinglish: Tum log online sabse zyada kahan time spend karte ho? Mujhe bhi samjhao, main thoda peeche hoon.
firstLine.hindi: तुम लोग ऑनलाइन सबसे ज़्यादा कहाँ समय बिताते हो? मुझे भी समझाओ, मैं थोड़ा पीछे हूँ।
firstLine.english: Where do you and your friends spend most of your time online? Teach me, I'm a bit behind.

followUps: Have you heard of anyone getting a weird message or a photo threat? What did they do?
If something like that happened to a friend, what would you tell them?
say: If anyone ever threatens you with a photo, come straight to me. You won't be in trouble.
It's never the fault of the person being threatened.
Even a fake photo can be reported and taken down. There's help for this.
avoid: Just don't post photos, then nothing will happen. (Fake images can be made from any normal photo.)
Threatening to take the phone away. Teens hide problems when they fear losing it.

react.quiet: That's okay. I just want you to know the door's open.
react.upset: I'm not accusing you of anything. I trust you. I just don't trust some people online.
react.disagree: You probably know more about this than me. Tell me what I've got wrong.
react.noTalk: Okay. Just remember: whatever happens online, you won't be in trouble for telling me.

cards.getHelp: if your teen is being blackmailed or threatened, or a fake or private image is shared → Cybercrime 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in, and Take It Down to remove images. Don't pay, don't delete messages (they're evidence), don't contact the person yourself, and don't blame your teen.
cards.sources: McAfee, Cyberbullying in Plain Sight, India 2022 · OECD AI incident report (IIIT Raipur), 2025

cards.name: Consent and personal safety
cards.teenQuestion: Is it okay to say no, even to someone you know?
cards.whyNow: Most people who harm children are known to them: about 97% of offenders in India's POCSO cases knew the child. Only 6 of 18 parents in our survey have talked about consent.

firstLine.hinglish: Kabhi aisa hua hai ki kisi friend ko kuch karne ka mann nahi tha, par woh mana nahi kar paaya? Log aisa kyun karte hain?
firstLine.hindi: कभी ऐसा हुआ है कि किसी दोस्त का कुछ करने का मन नहीं था, पर वह मना नहीं कर पाया? लोग ऐसा क्यों करते हैं?
firstLine.english: Has a friend ever not wanted to do something but couldn't say no? Why do you think people go along with it?

followUps: How can you tell when someone really means yes, and when they just feel they have to say it?
Who are the adults you'd feel okay going to if something felt wrong?
say: You won't be in trouble for telling me, whoever it's about.
You can say no to anyone, even family, teachers or friends, if something feels wrong.
Other people's no counts too. Asking first is always right.
avoid: Strangers are the danger. (Most harm comes from people a child knows.)
Blaming questions like "Why were you there?" or "What were you wearing?"
Respect your elders, do what they say, without exceptions for safety.

react.quiet: That's okay. I just want you to know you can always say no, and always tell me.
react.upset: I'm not worried about anything you did. I just want you to feel safe.
react.disagree: Tell me more. How do people your age think about it?
react.noTalk: Okay. Just remember: if anyone ever makes you uncomfortable, you can tell me, and you won't be in trouble.

cards.getHelp: if your teen tells you someone touched them, hurt them or made them feel unsafe → stay calm, believe them, and call Childline 1098, or 112 if they're in danger now. Don't confront the person yourself.
cards.sources: NCRB Crime in India 2024, POCSO data · Raise parent survey, 18 parents, Oct 2026

cards.name: Body and growing up
cards.teenQuestion: Is what's happening to my body normal?
cards.whyNow: Puberty questions are often left to school or friends. In a 2026 Bengaluru study, 52% of mothers had never talked about reproductive health with their daughters, and boys usually get even less guidance.
cards.whySource: Rashmi et al., Bengaluru, 2026 · Likith, Bengaluru, 2024

firstLine.hinglish: School mein body ke changes ke baare mein kuch padhaya hai? Kuch aisa hai jo unhone theek se nahi samjhaya?
firstLine.hindi: स्कूल में शरीर के बदलावों के बारे में कुछ पढ़ाया है? कुछ ऐसा है जो उन्होंने ठीक से नहीं समझाया?
firstLine.english: Has school taught anything about how bodies change? Anything they didn't explain properly?

followUps: What do people your age wonder about but feel too awkward to ask?
Where do your friends usually look up stuff like this?
say: You won't be in trouble for asking me anything.
Everyone's body changes at a different pace. There's no 'right' time.
If I don't know the answer, we'll look it up together, or ask a doctor.
avoid: Comments on their weight, skin or looks.
We don't talk about these things.
Giving medical advice yourself. For symptoms or worries, see a doctor.

react.quiet: It's a bit awkward for me too. We can keep it short.
react.upset: I'm sorry. I didn't mean to embarrass you. I just want you to have real answers.
react.disagree: Okay, tell me what you've heard. Let's figure out what's true.
react.noTalk: Okay. You can always ask me later, or text me if that's easier.

cards.getHelp: for any medical worry (pain, very irregular periods, anything that doesn't seem right) → a doctor. If your teen seems very unhappy with their body or stops eating properly → Tele-MANAS 14416.
cards.sources: Rashmi et al., parent-adolescent communication on SRH, Bengaluru, IJCMPH 2026 · Likith, factors influencing parent-adolescent SRH communication, 2024
